title: Unique scalar Roos comparison normalized by the universal derived unit
statement: For a scheme W and the constant integral coefficient ring of a finite extension E of Q_l, there is a unique natural isomorphism from the localized strict Roos complex to the actual total right-derived inverse limit [def-pur-compact-support-scalar-limit-maps, def-weil-strict-roos-model]. Its composite with the localized ordinary limit inclusion is the canonical limit-cone isomorphism followed by the universal derived-limit unit. All coefficient hypotheses and the normalization equation are exactly those of the attached Lean statement.

source.place: Tag 0941, computation of derived inverse limits by the strict Roos complex; universal normalization of the comparison in Step 3 of lem-pur-compact-support-scalar-limit-reduction.

proof.text: The canonical right-derived-limit unit is a right-derived functor unit. Transport it through the canonical isomorphism between the limit of tower complexes and degreewise limits [lem-sf-strict-roos-derived-limit-comparison]. Exact products in the coefficient module category follow from [det-pe-products-exact] via the existing scalarRoos_exactProducts theorem of [def-pur-compact-support-scalar-limit-maps].

Use the right-derived functor represented by the strict Roos complex [lem-weil-strict-roos-derivation]. Uniqueness of right-derived functors gives its comparison with the actual total right-derived limit. The defining equation for rightDerivedNatTrans proves its normalization on every complex. The canonical derived-unit API used for transport is the proved helper of [lem-pur-derived-square-normalization-naturality].

For another normalized comparison, compose it with the inverse Roos comparison and lift the resulting natural isomorphism through localization. Its composition with the Roos-derived unit agrees with that of the canonical comparison by the assumed normalization. Right-derived-functor extensionality makes the lifted comparison equal to the canonical one. Localized component equations then give equality of the original natural isomorphisms. This argument includes zero complexes and uses no arbitrary choices beyond the uniquely normalized derived comparison.

lean.statement:
theorem scalarRoosComparison_existsUnique (W : Scheme.{u}) :
    ∃! κ : roosF (A := Modules
        (ULift.{u + 1} (Padic.coefficientExtensionIntegers l E)) W) ⋙
          DerivedCategory.Q ≅ DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ scalarLimit l E W,
      ∀ K : CochainComplex (Towers
        (ULift.{u + 1} (Padic.coefficientExtensionIntegers l E)) W) ℤ,
        DerivedCategory.Q.map (roosι K) ≫ κ.hom.app K =
          DerivedCategory.Q.map
            (limit.isoLimitCone ⟨HomologicalComplex.coneOfHasLimitEval K.asFunctor,
              HomologicalComplex.isLimitConeOfHasLimitEval K.asFunctor⟩).hom ≫
            derivedUnit
              (lim : Towers (ULift.{u + 1} (Padic.coefficientExtensionIntegers l E)) W ⥤ _)
              K
